t:
(a) 
In General.—
Section 612 of the Trade Act of 1974 (19 U.S.C. 2486) is amended by inserting “(a)” before “It” and by adding at the end thereof the following:

“(b) 
The President shall study the desirability of entering into trade agreements with countries in the northern portion of the western hemisphere to promote the economic growth of the United States and such countries and the mutual expansion of market opportunities and report to the Committee on Ways and Means of the House of Representatives and the Committee on Finance of the Senate his findings and conclusions within 2 years after the date of enactment of this Act. The study shall include an examination of competitive opportunities and conditions of competition between such countries and the United States in the agricultural, energy, and other appropriate sectors.”.



 
    (b) 
Clerical Amendments.—

        (1) 
The caption of section 612 of such Act is amended to read as follows:


“SEC. 612. 
TRADE RELATIONS WITH NORTH AMERICAN COUNTRIES.”.



 
        (2) 
The table of contents of such Act is amended by striking out the item relating to section 612 and inserting in lieu thereof the following new item:


“Sec. 612. Trade relations with North American countries.”.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that a presidential study on trade agreements with other countries, plus a formal report, amounts to consultation. But the only recipients of the report are congressional committees, which are inside the federal government, and the study itself requires no input from states, the public, industry, or other outside parties. The remaining provisions are clerical amendments to a caption and table of contents.
fable.s: report to the Committee on Ways and Means of the House of Representatives and the Committee on Finance of the Senate his findings and conclusions

opus.w: The section requires only a presidential study and a report to two congressional committees, and both of those are inside the federal government. The reference to trade agreements with foreign countries is tempting, but it is just the subject of the study. Nothing requires consulting those countries or any other outside party before a federal decision. The remaining provisions are clerical amendments to a caption and a table of contents.
opus.s: The President shall study the desirability of entering into trade agreements with countries in the northern portion of the western hemisphere to promote the economic growth of the United States and such countries and the mutual expansion of market opportunities and report to the Committee on Ways and Means of the House of Representatives and the Committee on Finance of the Senate his findings and conclusions
opus.b:
I think the answer is No.

**The tempting misreading:** The section talks about "trade agreements with countries in the northern portion of the western hemisphere." Foreign countries are outside the federal government, so this can look like outside involvement. It isn't. The section only requires the President to *study whether* such agreements are desirable. No foreign government, state, company or member of the public is asked for input on any federal decision.

**What the section actually does:** It requires the President to run a study and report the findings to the House Ways and Means Committee and the Senate Finance Committee. Congressional committees are inside the federal government. The rest of the section is clerical renaming.

qwen_chat.w: This section requires the President to conduct a study and report the findings to Congress. Both the President and Congress are inside the federal government. There is no requirement to consult with outside parties, such as the foreign countries mentioned, the general public, or advisory committees. The mention of foreign countries is the subject of the study, not participants in the decision-making process.
qwen_chat.s: The President shall study the desirability of entering into trade agreements with countries in the northern portion of the western hemisphere to promote the economic growth of the United States and such countries and the mutual expansion of market opportunities and report to the Committee on Ways and Means of the House of Representatives and the Committee on Finance of the Senate his findings and conclusions within 2 years after the date of enactment of this Act.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the study involves "countries in the northern portion of the western hemisphere," implying consultation with foreign governments. However, the text only mandates a study *by* the President and a report *to* Congress. It does not explicitly require the President to consult with those foreign countries or any other outside entities during the study process. The interaction described is internal (President studying) and internal (reporting to Congress).
